card: This pull request decouples the wallet database client version record from the Bitcoin Core node version and adds records tracking the feature flags of the last client to open and decrypt the wallet. It enables future wallet upgrades to detect upgrade-downgrade-upgrade scenarios and re-run automatic upgrade logic without leaving wallets in an inconsistent state. Because this tracking metadata must be established in released versions before any automatic upgrades can safely rely on it, it serves as a foundation for downstream wallet upgrades such as PR 33034.
changed_since_previous: The PR now updates legacy wallet migration logic to record the last opened version, opened features, and decrypted features when migrating a wallet.

enables: Future automatic wallet upgrades requiring downgrade detection

evidence: The PR description explains that writing this tracking metadata into wallet databases must be deployed prior to releasing features that introduce new automatic upgrades: 'in order for this to work, we need to have implemented writing such information into versions prior to the ones which introduce new automatic upgrades.'
PR #33034 is based on this pull request.
problem: When a wallet is opened or modified by an older software release after an automatic upgrade, and subsequently re-opened in a newer release, it can accumulate mixed upgraded and non-upgraded data. The wallet currently lacks a reliable mechanism to detect upgrade-downgrade-upgrade cycles and determine whether automatic upgrades need to be reapplied.

risk.why: A flaw in database version record migration or failure to handle record writes could corrupt wallet metadata or prevent a wallet from loading.

summary: This pull request decouples the wallet database version record from the node client version and introduces two new database records: LAST_OPENED_FEATURES and LAST_DECRYPTED_FEATURES. These feature bit flags track the automatic upgrade capabilities of the last client that opened or unlocked/decrypted the wallet file, allowing future releases to detect when a wallet was used in an older software release and re-run necessary automatic upgrades.
